title: Reconstruction from lower truncations under ringed-site local bounds
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ be a weak Serre subcategory: it is strictly full, contains zero, and is closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between its objects and under extensions. Write $D_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$ for complexes whose every cohomology sheaf lies in $\mathcal S$, and $D^+_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$ for its bounded-below part. Suppose there is a set $\mathcal V\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ such that every object has a covering by members of $\mathcal V$. For every $V\in\mathcal V$ suppose there are an integer $d_V$ and a cofinal collection of covering families $\{V_i\to V\}$ such that $H^p(V_i,F)=0$ for every $p>d_V$ and $F\in\mathcal S$. Cofinal means every covering has a refinement in the collection, and $H^p(V_i,F)$ is the right derived functor of sections. Use the resolution-derived inverse limit on strict inverse sequences, whose underlying object has the Roos triangle [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], [def-weil-derived-limit]. For every $E\in D_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$, the canonical lower-truncation maps [def-kun-truncations] induce an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O)$
$$E\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_{n\geq0}\tau_{\geq-n}E.$$
This isomorphism is compatible with every canonical projection to $\tau_{\geq-n}E$.

source.place: Tag 0D6S, lemma-olsson-laszlo, statement and proof; local bound hypotheses spelled out from situation-olsson-laszlo

proof.text: Choose a complex $A^\bullet$ representing $E$ and form the strict tower $T_n=\tau_{\geq-n}A^\bullet$ using the kernel/cokernel formulas of [def-kun-truncations]. Its quotient maps $c_n:A^\bullet\to T_n$ and transitions $u_n:T_{n+1}\to T_n$ satisfy $u_nc_{n+1}=c_n$ degreewise. Truncation gives $H^j(T_n)=0$ for $j<-n$ and $H^j(c_n)$ an isomorphism for $j\geq-n$. Thus $T_n\in D^+_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$: its cohomology is zero or isomorphic to a cohomology sheaf of $E$, and $\mathcal S$ contains zero and is strictly full. For $n_j=\max(0,-j)$ and $n\geq n_j$, the equality $H^j(u_n)H^j(c_{n+1})=H^j(c_n)$ makes $H^j(u_n)$ an isomorphism.

Let $L=R\varprojlim_nT_n$ be the resolution-derived limit in the statement. The strict-tower theorem gives its natural Roos triangle $L\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\to L[1]$, with $P=\prod_n^D T_n$. Set $p_n=\operatorname{pr}_np$. The product property gives $a:E\to P$ with $\operatorname{pr}_na=c_n$. Compatibility gives $\operatorname{pr}_n(1-s)a=c_n-u_nc_{n+1}=0$ for every $n$, hence $(1-s)a=0$. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(E,-)$ in this triangle supplies $c:E\to L$ with $pc=a$, hence $p_nc=c_n$ for every $n$. This also verifies existence of a comparison with all the required projections. The following argument proves invertibility for every such comparison, in particular for the one obtained from the stipulated resolution construction.

source.place: Tag 0H72, remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations; the Roos triangle is supplied by the strict resolution construction

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-local-bound-stationary-limit-cohomology] to the strict tower $(T_n,u_n)$. Its site, ring sheaf, weak Serre subcategory, covering set, cofinal collections and integers $d_V$ are exactly those of the item; step 1 verifies bounded-below membership separately for every $n$ and stabilization in each degree $j$ at $n_j$. Therefore the actual projection induces an isomorphism $H^j(p_n):H^j(L)\to H^j(T_n)$ for every $n\geq n_j$. No uniform lower bound on the tower and no exactness of products is required by that cited statement.

Fix $j$ and take $n=n_j$. Applying the cohomology functor to $p_nc=c_n$ gives $H^j(p_n)H^j(c)=H^j(c_n)$. Both $H^j(p_n)$ and $H^j(c_n)$ are isomorphisms by steps 1 and 3, so $H^j(c)=H^j(p_n)^{-1}H^j(c_n)$ is an isomorphism. This calculation concerns the specified comparison $c$, rather than merely an unspecified isomorphism between its source and target.

The module-sheaf category is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], using precisely the coefficient-relative smallness assumption in the item. Since $H^j(c)$ is an isomorphism for every integer $j$, [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] makes $c$ an isomorphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category. The identities $p_nc=c_n$ from step 2 hold for every $n$, including those below the stabilization index, and give the asserted compatibility with every canonical projection.

reviewed_lean.note: Only change is the item's lean record; the statement is verbatim in the file. All hypotheses match Stacks 0D6R/0D6S and the node: per-V d before the covering quantifier, refinement by factorization through a covering member, vanishing uniform over F and p>d, all five weak Serre conditions, homologyProperty, cohomology as sections of a K-injective resolution. Truncations are the DerivedCategory.TStructure.t truncGE maps named in the def-kun-truncations docstring, with transitions n+1→n. Conclusion: an isomorphism E≅L compatible with every projection, and every compatible comparison c is invertible. Quantifying over any derived-limit triangle instead of only the resolution-built one is slightly more general and still true (0H72; such limits are isomorphic compatibly with the projections). Edge cases E=0, S=0, n=0, negative d, empty coverings and independent universes checked; no extra hypotheses; no duplicate (0D6P uniform-bound and pointwise variants differ).
